nodes.name: 16.8-nm Pd cubic seeds synthesis
nodes.procedure: An 8-ml aqueous solution containing AA (60 mg), PVP (105 mg), and KBr (600 mg) is added to a 23-ml vial. Subsequently, the solution undergoes preheating at 80°C for 10 min. Following the preheating step, a one-shot injection of 3-ml Na₂PdCl₄ aqueous solution with a concentration of 19 mg/ml is added into the vial in one shot. The reaction mixture is capped and kept at 80°C for 3 hours under magnetic stirring and then cooled to room temperature. The Pd cubic seeds are dispersed in Oam solvent after a cleaning procedure involving centrifugation and washing with DI water three times.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of 16.8-nm Pd cubic seeds... An 8-ml aqueous solution containing AA (60 mg), PVP (105 mg), and KBr (600 mg)

nodes.name: Epitaxial growth PtRuFeCoNi atomic layers on Pd cubic seeds
nodes.procedure: A total of 0.5 ml of OAm solution containing Pd cubic seeds is mixed with 3 ml of ODE in a 23-ml vial. Then, the mixture is preheated at 110°C for 20 min under magnetic stirring, followed by an increase to 200°C for 20 min. Subsequently, a 14-ml precursor solution containing H₂PtCl₆·6H₂O, RuCl₃·xH₂O, Ni(C₅H₇O₂)₂, Co(C₅H₇O₂)₂, and Fe(C₅H₇O₂)₃, each with an equal molar concentration of 0.042 μmol ml⁻¹ in OAm, is prepared. Using a syringe pump, this precursor solution is then added dropwise to the reaction mixture containing Pd seeds at a constant injection rate of 0.8 ml hour⁻¹. After the precursor solution has been added, the reaction mixture is kept at 200°C for another 1 hour. After that, the Pd@PtRuFeCoNi core-shell nanocrystals are collected through centrifugation and washing with n-hexane three times and redispersed in DI water.

nodes.name: 12-nm Pd nanocubes synthesis
nodes.procedure: An 8 ml aqueous solution containing AA (60 mg), PVP (105 mg), and KBr (300 mg) is introduced into a 23-ml vial. The solution is subsequently preheated at 80°C for 10 min. Following the preheating step, a one-shot injection of 3-ml Na₂PdCl₄ aqueous solution with a concentration of 19 mg/ml is added into the vial in one shot. The reaction mixture is capped and kept at 80°C for 3 hour under magnetic stirring and then cooled to room temperature. After the reaction, the Pd nanocubes are dispersed in EG solvent after a cleaning procedure including centrifugation and washing with DI water three times.

nodes.name: 18.1-nm Pd octahedral seeds
nodes.procedure: Three-hundred microliters of the 12-nm Pd nanocubes with a concentration of 1.8 mg ml⁻¹ are mixed with 8 ml of an aqueous mixture containing 100 μl of HCHO and PVP (105 mg) in a 23-ml vial. The solution is subsequently preheated at 60°C for 10 min. Following the preheating step, a one-shot injection of 3 ml Na₂PdCl₄ aqueous solution with a concentration of 12.6 mg/ml is added into the vial in one shot. The reaction mixture is capped and kept at 60°C for 3 hours under magnetic stirring and then cooled to room temperature. After the reaction, the Pd octahedral seeds are dispersed in Oam after a cleaning procedure involving centrifugation and washing with DI water three times.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals retention of cubic shape after PtRuFeCoNi deposition with edge length increased to 18.4 nm, indicating ~1.0 nm thick shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM image reveals good retention of cubic shape after the deposition (Fig. 1C). The edge length of Pd@PtRuFeCoNi core-shell nanocubes is increased to 18.4 nm (Fig. 1I), indicating around 1.0-nm thickness of PtRuFeCoNi shell layers.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows periodic lattice extending across whole nanocube with ~1 nm outer surface contrast difference due to atomic number variation; lattice spacing of (200) plane is 0.20 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM image taken from an individual nanocube reveals the periodic lattice extending across the whole nanocube covered by {100} facets, suggesting the epitaxial growth mode (Fig. 1D). ... The lattice spacing of (200) plane is around 0.20 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms FCC phase diffraction peaks shifted to lower 2θ values compared to Pd nanocubes; FWHM = 1.01° larger than Pd nanocubes (0.81°).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis also confirms the diffraction peaks of the FCC phase (Fig. 1H). When compared to that of Pd nanocubes, the diffraction peaks of the Pd@PtRuFeCoNi core-shell nanocubes shift toward lower 2θ values.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mappings and line scans verify core-shell distribution with Pd core and solid-solution shell of five elements; lower IGM signals vs PGMs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive x-ray spectrometry (EDS) elemental mappings (Fig. 1G) and their corresponding line scan profiles (fig. S8) verify the spatial core-shell distributions of Pd@PtRuFeCoNi nanocubes.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms PtRuFeCoNi atomic percentages: Pt 20%, Ru 22%, Fe 21%, Co 19%, Ni 18%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic percentages of Pt, Ru, Fe, Co, and Ni elements are 20, 22, 21, 19, and 18% respectively, confirmed by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) analysis (Fig. 1J).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows coexistence of metal and oxidized states for all elements; more Ru⁴⁺, Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺, Co³⁺/Co²⁺, Ni²⁺ due to surface oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The coexistence of metal and oxidation states is identified by the XPS spectra with curve fittings for all elements, which can be attributed to the spontaneous oxidation on the outermost surface of IGM-PGM-HEA when exposed to air.

nodes.characterization_summary: Synchrotron XAS reveals coordination environments and atomic mixing: XANES shows orbital hybridizations of mixed elements; FT-EXAFS fitting gives Pt-5d radial distance 2.733 Å (CN 2.36), Pt-4d 2.716 Å (CN 2.94), Pt-3d 2.674 Å (CN 1.81) confirming random distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The post-edges of all elements exhibit deviations in shape and intensity compared to their foil and oxide counterparts, implying the orbital hybridizations of the mixed elements... On the basis of the fitting results (table S6), the radial distance of Pt within the PtRuFeCoNi atomic layers is around 2.733Å (Pt-5d)... coordination values of Pt-5d, Pt-4d, and Pt-3d are calculated as 2.36, 2.94, and 1.81, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ heating shows phase transformation: random mixing (25°C) → L1₀-ordered (300°C) → L1₂-ordered (400°C) → phase-separated (500°C) confirming metastable nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We reveal the transformation kinetics of phase from high-entropy mixing (25°C), to ordered L1₀ (300°C) and L1₂ (400°C) intermetallic, and to phase-separated phases (500°C), indicating the metastable phase of the far-from-equilibrium PtRuFeCoNi atomic layers.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM, FFT patterns, and EDS confirm all 10 IGM-PGM-HEA atomic layers (PtIrFeCoNi, PtPdFeCoNi, etc.) have cubic shape, {100} facets, ultrathin shells (~5 atomic layers) with homogeneous elemental distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the TEM, HAADF-STEM images, and FFT patterns, these Pd@IGM-PGM-HEA core-shell nanocubes all have a cubic shape and {100} facets, together with ultrathin shells. The corresponding EDS maps, line scan, and ICP-OES analysis confirm that the deposited five IGM-PGM elements... are distributed throughout the entire shells.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM identifies L1₂-ordered crystal lattices (PGM:IGM = 3:1) in local regions of PtRhFeCoNi, RhRuFeCoNi, IrRhFeCoNi shells with additional (100)/(110) superlattice spots in FFT.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the PtRhFeCoNi (Fig. 3G), RhRuFeCoNi (Fig. 3H), and IrRhFeCoNi (Fig. 3I), the L1₂-ordered crystal lattices... in some local regions of shells highlighted in red squares are also identified by the HAADF-STEM images... The corresponding FFT patterns... confirm the presence of additional (100) and (110) superlattice spots.
